title: Family silence about the past; learning she was born out of wedlock
summary: Her family never talked about backgrounds, so she listened under the bed. A relative's angry remark at 10 or 12 told her she was illegitimate; she shrugged it off and went out to play.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: No. I'm from a family that never talked much about backgrounds and what-not, except for a few things that I learned from them at an early age. I used to, as a young kid, I'd sneak under the bed and listen to their conversation and I learned a great deal about the past through that. They never allowed the kids to sit in on conversations when they had company or anything like that.
But this was not in relation to your father?
No, I never knew about him at all. I never knew that I was born out of wedlock until I was 10 or 12 years
old and a relative of mine got angry with me and said, 'You grew up like a weed. You don't even belong to the family,' or something like that. Then I discovered it.
I felt very discouraged but I've always been a strong person. I've never allowed anything to linger long with me to make me feel unhappy. I'd turn it off and go out and play or do something.
